articles.title: KradleBench: Multi-agent AI evals in Minecraft
articles.content: Hi HN -This is James and Kemal. In past lives we led Firebase and Tensorflow/JAX respectively. HN has been a particularly big part of my (James’) career and the trajectory I’ve taken would be meaningfully different without it. Thank you!Our team shipped a benchmark: KradleBench. We test AI in Minecraft Worlds.1. The worlds are multi-agent. Humans and other AIs are in there too, often pursuing their own goals. Collaboration and conflict skills fall out of this property.2. The world are dynamic. They constantly change, which means that agents need to react. “Capture the Flag” has a single winning condition, and many different ways to achieve it. This leads to many emergent and creative strategies.3. The worlds are real-time. They are not turn-based, they do not wait for AIs to finish thinking. articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，今年 10 月底，华为 WATCH 5 系列、ULTIMATE DESIGN 星钻绽放等手表开启 HarmonyOS 7 花粉 Beta 版招募。随后 7.0.0.107 SP18 版本开启推送。但据用户反馈，部分设备更新后出现 BUG，因此升级活动暂缓。IT之家注意到，华为官方最新宣布，HarmonyOS 7.0.0.107SP41 版本开始分批推送给花粉 Beta 版升级尝鲜报名入选成功的 WATCH 5 系列用户。适配机型HUAWEI WATCH 5 42mm（含十周年款）（SOC-AL00）HUAWEI WATCH 5 46mm（含十周年款）（RTS-AL00）版本更新日志6.1.0.330SP18/6.1.0.330SP22/6.1.0.333/6.1.0.335 → 7.0.0.107SP41 更新点：1. 系统界面全面焕新，表盘与多任务列表等融入灵动光影，为您呈现更精致、流畅的交互体验2. 新增 HarmonyOS 7 光穹表盘，柔和流光漫过盘面，光影层次细腻通透，将静谧和灵动凝于腕间3. 健康三叶草升级为健康生活应用，新增饮食维度，在华为运动健康应用配置相关打卡任务后，即可解锁四叶草模型，多维度助您养成健康生活好习惯4. 增强录音机同步能力，支持录音文件同步至安卓、iOS 手机的华为运动健康应用，可在华为运动健康应用 > 设备 > 录音机查看 (请将华为运动健康应用更新至最新版本)5. 负一屏小艺建议新增支持通知摘要、重要日、通勤概况等主题，为您提供更加场景化的智能服务 (配对 HarmonyOS 6 及以上版本的手机支持，且需前往手机应用市场将智慧分发服务更新至 6.0.8.400 及以上版本)6. 支持 AI 通话降噪，蓝牙通话时，即使周边嘈杂，对方也能清晰听到您的声音7. 支持同步 HarmonyOS 7 及以上版本手机的地震预警消息，及时通知提升安全保障8. 设置中“常亮显示”更名为“熄屏显示”参考IT之家此前报道，华为官方 11 月 11 日发布《HUAWEI WATCH 5 系列 HarmonyOS 7 花粉 Beta 版本升级进展通报》。其中提到，针对大家反馈的高端精致类、特性体验优化类、系统稳定性等问题，已收到，研发团队正在紧急攻关打磨质量。同时，花粉 Beta 待版本充分测试验证后，将尽快分批推送。相关阅读：《华为 WATCH 5 系列、ULTIMATE DESIGN 星钻绽放等手表开启 HarmonyOS 7 花粉 Beta 版招募》《华为 WATCH 5 系列开推 HarmonyOS 7 花粉 Beta 版，新增 AI 通话降噪、同步手机地震预警消息等》《华为通报 WATCH 5 系列 HarmonyOS 7 花粉 Beta 版本升级进展：待充分测试验证后，将尽快分批推送》

articles.title: Show HN: Klistra – A complete studio for spec-driven AI motion design and video
articles.content: As a solo-dev with a lot of projects going on, I found myself needing to make short promos or explainer videos. Not being familiar with animation software, I had the idea to use Claude to code up those videos and export them as video files. Note that this was before AI-coded music videos went viral, back in the early days when the models were just getting good enough to make the result actually look good.In the process of creating these clips I stumbled into a bunch of bugs and setup needed to make it work reliably. The list of features I wanted for better control and feedback kept growing and I needed to sign up for a bunch of services to get music, voiceovers and other media into my project. I couldn't find an existing service that had everything I wanted. Seeing these hurdles and that the technology was only easily accessible to people already confident with coding agents, I started working on Klistra, and a couple of months later I'm turning it into a service so you all can use it

articles.title: 腾讯：更多企业转向国产芯片，将助推国内供应链建设提速
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，腾讯昨日发布第三季度财报。财报显示，其第三季度实现营收 2073.36 亿元，同比增长 8%；毛利 1159.11 亿元，同比增长 7%；归母净利润为 636.12 亿元，同比增长 0.8%。据《科创板日报》报道，对于持续增加的 AI 投入，腾讯管理层在业绩会上表示，公司当前资本开支主要用于 AI 基础设施建设。这类投入并非一次性消耗，建成后的基础设施可以持续用于模型训练和 Token 生成。随着 2026 年、2027 年建设的基础设施在后续年份发挥作用，预计到 2028 年相关投入带来的经营压力有望逐步缓解。管理层同时提到，AI 基础设施的投入成本未来有望出现积极变化。其认为，目前设备采购价格相对较高，预计到 2028 年，同类设备采购价格将明显下降；此外，更重要的是模型训练和推理的计算效率持续提升，在相同基础设施条件下，未来有望完成更多训练任务、处理更多 Token。算力供给仍是当前 AI 业务面临的现实约束。谈及最新收紧限制的影响，腾讯高管表示，短期内实际可用算力减少，无论租赁还是自建算力都受到影响，模型训练也将承压。腾讯目前混元 Hy4 采用的精度训练效率较高，但下一代模型的推出可能需要更长时间。该高管同时表示，从长期看，相关限制可能推动更多中国企业转向国内供应链和国产芯片，带动国内供应链建设提速，相关研发力量也将进一步向这一领域集中。另据IT之家昨晚报道，腾讯控股在 2026 年第三季度财报沟通中披露，受芯片限制影响，训练下一代模型将需要更长时间。腾讯表示，通过加大投入，向上探索大模型智能上限，向下构建覆盖个人生活、办公协作和企业生产的 AI 应用体系，腾讯正加速推进 AI 化变革，向 AI 引领的科技公司迈进。相关阅读：《腾讯：受芯片限制影响，训练下一代模型将需要更长时间》

articles.title: 非洲加速向 5G-A 网络演进：华为 × Vodacom 联合发布 U6GHz“黄金频段”创新成果
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据“华为无线网络”公众号分享，在南非开普敦通信网络展览会（Africa Tech Festival 2026）期间，华为联合南非领先运营商 Vodacom 发布了 U6GHz 创新成果，为非洲市场 U6GHz 商用落地奠定了技术与场景基础。据介绍，U6GHz（6425–7125MHz）是继 C-band 之后又一备受关注的大带宽频段，也是 Sub-10GHz 范围内最后一块 700MHz 级连续大带宽频谱资源，被业界视为“黄金频段”。WRC-23 已将其正式标识为 IMT 频谱，覆盖全球 80% 人口所在市场，全球已有超 20 个国家和地区完成频谱标识与分配。然而，频率越高、路径损耗越大，U6GHz 与 C-Band 之间存在约 13dB 的覆盖差距。传统方案需新增一倍站点数量或大幅提升发射功率才能实现同覆盖部署，使得建设成本与工程实施均不具备商用可行性。针对这一产业难题，华为推出业界首款 U6GHz 商用设备 VitaAAU。该设备搭载华为首创的 RetinaMIMO 技术，通过 TTI 级波束扫描系统重构射频链路拓扑，解决立体覆盖坍缩难题；通过重构天面阵列架构，解决阵列增长时增益边际效益递减的问题。IT之家从华为官方获悉，VitaAAU 覆盖范围较业界 1024 阵子方案提升约 30%，可实现 U6GHz 与 C-Band 在水平和垂直方向上的覆盖能力对齐，辅助运营商实现共站同覆盖部署，同时降低 30% 能耗。基于华为创新技术方案，Vodacom 工程团队在 VDC Lab 中完成了 U6GHz 端到端技术验证 —— 聚焦 U6GHz FWA（固定无线接入）核心场景，覆盖从云游戏、实时直播、企业视频会议等应用场景，主打超大带宽和低时延特性。值得一提的是，U6GHz 既可以服务于 5G-A 网络增强，也被视为面向 6G 的核心候选频段。Vodacom 接入网工程管理执行总监 Diane Keitsemore 表示，通过 U6GHz 可以把更优质的网络体验带给每一个人，缩小数字鸿沟，助力加速向 5G-A 网络演进。

articles.title: 消息称 Anthropic 考虑扩大 IPO 规模，散户认购意向接近千亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，北京时间今天（18 日）晚间，据美国 CNBC 援引知情人士消息称，Anthropic 考虑扩大 IPO 发行规模，并可能将发行价定在远高于 80 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 534.4 元人民币）的水平。当地时间 17 日，Anthropic 结束了认购意向征集，汇总了投资者需求，为登陆纳斯达克做准备。知情人士称，机构投资者的认购意向总额约为 4,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 2.67 万亿元人民币），散户认购意向也接近 1,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 6,679.86 亿元人民币）。不过，这些认购意向并不具有约束力，发行方案仍可能调整。知情人士透露，Anthropic 将在当地时间 18 日下午作出最终决定，预计在当天美股收盘后敲定 IPO 发行价。Anthropic 此次 IPO 的认购需求超过了 SpaceX，尽管后者的发行规模更大。SpaceX 今年 6 月登陆纳斯达克，最终募资 857 亿美元（现汇率约合 5,724.64 亿元人民币），创下全球 IPO 规模纪录。Anthropic 上周公布的发行方案显示，公司计划发行 8.25 亿股股票，每股定价 70 至 78 美元（现汇率约合 467.6 至 521 元人民币），按发行价上限计算，募资额最高可达 643.5 亿美元（现汇率约合 4,298.49 亿元人民币）。Anthropic 上市也是 AI 行业面临的一次重要考验。近期，AI 行业接连受到冲击：美国中期选举过程中强烈反对浪潮不断，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋上周被免职。Anthropic 与全球多家科技巨头有着密切的商业往来，既有投资和合作，也涉及产品采购。亚马逊和谷歌所持 Anthropic 股份的价值均超过 1,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 6,679.86 亿元人民币）；谷歌、微软、英伟达和 AMD 等公司还同意合计投入 260 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,736.76 亿元人民币）认购此次 IPO。另一方面，Anthropic 也向英伟达、谷歌、亚马逊和 AMD 采购价格高昂的计算系统。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据界面新闻今日报道，小米创办人、董事长兼 CEO 雷军在 APEC 圆桌会谈的采访中披露未发布新机小米 18 相关信息。这款机型预计 12 月正式发布，硬件层面沿用小米数字标准版小机身，性能、影像、续航、屏幕等实现升级。报道还提到，有消息称新机起售价为 5699 元。据IT之家此前报道，小米 18 标准版手机已通过 3C 认证，相关页面显示会支持 100W 快充。爆料称，小米 18 会搭载骁龙 8 Elite Gen6 处理器、200MP 相机传感器，并配备 7200mAh 电池。目前，官方暂未确认小米 18 标准版配置信息，一切以官方为准。博主 @数码闲聊站 爆料称，小米 18 标准版定价在 6000 元左右，有超大的影像模组，号称屏幕 / 性能 / 影像全都领跑，是“26 年最后一款超模旗舰”、“米 6 之后最强标准版”、“等等党的终极胜利”。

articles.title: 一款路由器故障导致全美航班停飞，FAA 停用 60 余台设备并叫停后续安装
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，当地时间 17 日，据《纽约时报》报道，美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）宣布，将暂停安装慧与旗下瞻博网络生产的一款路由器。据了解，该设备原本用于美国航空设施的现代化改造，当前被 FAA 认为是 11 月 13 日全美航班暂停起飞的主要原因之一。FAA 不仅叫停了后续安装，还停用了此前部署的 60 多台路由器。美国交通部长肖恩 · 达菲最初将此次大规模停飞归咎于硬件老化，但第二天又透露，故障实际上与美国航空设施的升级改造有关。达菲介绍，事发时，科技公司 L3Harris 的一名承包商工作人员在阿肯色州埃尔多拉多的一处 FAA 设施内，准备将老旧的铜线通信线路更换为光纤，并安装新路由器。但新设备开始向空管系统中的其他路由器大量发送数据，得克萨斯州阿马里洛的另一台路由器也出现异常。随后，FAA 停用了这两台路由器。据悉，这款路由器在投入安装前经过了一年的测试。达菲在新闻发布会上解释说：“之前 68 次都没有出问题。但这台路由器开始向我们的网络大量发送数据，最终导致网络过载。”航空系统中的路由器主要负责传输雷达数据、飞行计划和天气信息等。确认路由器引发了故障后，FAA 局长布莱恩 · 贝德福德透露的信息仍是具体原因未查明。美国参议院商务、科学和交通委员会的民主党议员要求 FAA 查清路由器为何发生异常，并向国会说明将采取哪些措施，防止类似事故重演。达菲透露，国家安全机构告诉他，故障并非网络攻击造成，即便如此，自己仍要求 FBI 参与调查阿肯色州的故障路由器。达菲还再次敦促国会追加 500 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 3,339.93 亿元人民币）拨款，推进美国空管系统现代化改造。“我想告诉大家，继续使用这个破旧不堪的网络，只会让系统越来越不安全。改造工作必须完成。继续沿用旧系统，风险只会越来越大；只有修复系统，才能降低风险。”相关阅读：《导致全美航班停飞的“罪魁祸首”找到了？FAA 调查指向 20 年历史路由器》

articles.title: 数毛社实测《GTA 6》Xbox 版：Series X 稳定 30 帧，Series S 掉帧明显
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，数毛社（Digital Foundry）发布了两段视频，对《GTA 6》在不同主机上的性能表现进行了详细分析。其中一段重点测试 PlayStation 5 和 PS5 Pro 版本，另一段则针对 Xbox Series X 和 Series S 版本。IT之家注意到，对于 Xbox Series X 版，数毛社给出了相对积极的评价。该版本的表现与标准版 PS5 比较接近，内部渲染分辨率基本维持在 1440p，目标帧率为 30 FPS，不过在场景较为复杂、负载较高时，仍然会出现掉帧。数毛社分析师奥利弗 · 麦肯齐（Oliver Mackenzie）在视频中表示：“《GTA 6》在常规游戏过程中基本能够达到并维持 30 FPS，即使在激烈战斗和快速移动等高负载场景中，也能保持约 33 毫秒的帧时间。在 Xbox Series X 上，我体验的大多数战斗场景都能稳定运行在 30 FPS，掉帧情况相对较少。过场动画的表现也不错，没有出现动画卡顿。”他补充道：“在单人剧情过程中，玩家可能会在一些特别激烈的追逐战或枪战中遇到掉帧。不过，在绝大多数时间里，Xbox Series X 都能提供稳定的 30 FPS 游戏体验。”至于 Xbox Series S 版本，麦肯齐认为，经过硬件性能妥协后的游戏在基础画面表现方面“相当有意思”。一些理论上对处理器性能要求较高的技术，例如角色头发丝渲染和光线追踪反射，并没有从 Series S 版本中删减。他说：“从整体上看，游戏画面确实与 Series X 版本相当接近。不过，玩家会看到一系列幅度较小的画面缩水。”具体包括光照精度降低、反射效果更加模糊，以及阴影表现更加粗糙。他还表示：“画面分辨率也有所下降。根据我的测算，Series S 的内部渲染分辨率为 720p，而 Series X 为 1440p。不过，最终输出画面的效果远好于内部渲染分辨率所暗示的水平。与 Series X 相比，两者在画面锐度和细节方面的差距相对没有那么明显。”在总结画面表现时，麦肯齐表示：“Series S 版本确实削减了不少视觉效果，我怀疑还有一些明显的画面降级是我没有注意到的。但游戏的核心内容得到了保留，这一点确实超出了我的预期。“Series S 运行的仍然是大家熟悉的《GTA 6》，而且与我们经常在其他 AAA 级游戏的 Series S 版本中看到的画质妥协相比，这款游戏所做的取舍并没有想象中那么大。”不过，麦肯齐指出，这种画面表现的代价也不小。Xbox Series S 版《GTA 6》存在严重的帧率问题。尽管游戏仍以 30 FPS 为目标，但在大量常规游戏场景中，帧率都会跌破这一水平。他解释称：“即使只是驾驶速度较慢的汽车进行普通移动，游戏帧率也会长时间徘徊在 20 多帧的中后段。普通战斗场景中的帧率则基本会一直维持在 20 多帧。实际上，任何需要大量 AI 运算或资源动态加载的场景，都会拖累微软这款入门级主机的性能。”他补充道：“当然，我认为游戏大多数时候的实际帧率可能仍维持在 30 帧，因此表现也并非全无可取之处。过场动画通常运行正常，普通步行探索也基本没有太大问题。“但只要涉及战斗或者高速移动，帧率就会明显下滑。如果进一步挑战游戏的性能极限，在特别复杂的场景中，帧率最低甚至会降至约 20 FPS。”尽管如此，麦肯齐仍然对 Rockstar 为 Xbox Series S 开发这一版本的工作表示赞赏。他认为，Rockstar 成功将原本针对 PS5 和 Xbox Series X 打造的庞大游戏，移植到了性能弱得多的硬件上。即使是一些游戏规模远小于《GTA 6》的作品，其他开发商在适配 Series S 时也曾遇到不少困难。麦肯齐表示：“Rockstar 打造了一个相当忠实于原作设计理念的 Series S 版本，游戏的核心技术也都以相对合理的形式保留了下来。但 Series S 版本的帧率表现确实不理想，因此目前我建议玩家优先选择其他主机平台游玩。”“我很想知道，《GTA 6》在主机上的性能表现未来会如何变化，也希望 Series S 版本能够在后续更新中得到改善。不过，就目前而言，Series S 版本确实很难成为我的推荐选择。”目前还不清楚 Rockstar 能在游戏发售后将 Xbox Series S 版的性能提升到什么程度。不过，上个月微软宣布，Xbox Series X/S 主机以及 Xbox ROG Ally X 掌机将在未来的一次系统更新中获得 AMD 最新的 FSR 4.1 图像超分技术。与英伟达的 DLSS 技术类似，FSR 4.1 的主要优势在于，开发者可以先以较低分辨率渲染游戏画面，再利用 FSR articles.title: 哈啰调整 Robotaxi 组织架构：整合成立“模型开发与数据闭环部”，由 CEO 杨磊直接负责
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据蓝鲸汽车从哈啰方面确认，哈啰 Robotaxi 近期完成了一轮内部组织架构调整。原智能车-模型开发、系统方案与评测以及 AI Infra-数据平台等相关团队被整合成立“模型开发与数据闭环部”，由哈啰 CEO 杨磊直接负责。这一部门下设模型开发部与数据闭环部。与此同时，AI 原生车、二代车和量产工程交付的相关业务由 CTO 于乾坤负责。智能车其余部门架构及汇报线保持不变。此前，哈啰 Robotaxi 传出核心算法人才加盟的消息。哈啰方面确认，此前任职于具身智能公司无界动力的李一贤，目前确实已加入了哈啰 Robotaxi。据IT之家此前报道，2025 年 6 月，哈啰宣布进军 Robotaxi 赛道，由哈啰、蚂蚁集团、宁德时代通过旗下投资主体共同发起成立的“造父智能科技有限公司”正式注册。2025 年 9 月，哈啰宣布旗下 Robotaxi 业务获得阿里巴巴集团战略投资。今年 9 月，哈啰 Robotaxi 宣布完成约 1 亿美金（现汇率约合 6.67 亿元人民币）新一轮融资。本轮融资由上海国投先导基金领投，闵金投、创世伙伴创投跟投，投后估值接近 30 亿美元（现汇率约合 200 亿元人民币）。据了解，本轮资金将主要用于持续的研发投入，重点布局万卡集群算力平台、AI 大模型端到端技术迭代，以及高质量数据供应链体系建设。

articles.title: 马斯克“怒怼”奥尔特曼：SpaceX 预计不会从 OpenAI 处获得任何收入
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，SpaceX CEO 埃隆 · 马斯克出人意料地透露，公司在业务预测中并未考虑来自 OpenAI 的任何收入。此前，OpenAI CEO 萨姆 · 奥尔特曼谈及半导体行业可能重复计算 AI 芯片需求的问题。两人长期以来一直在 OpenAI 的发展定位上存在分歧。奥尔特曼暗示市场可能存在一定程度的产能过剩，马斯克的回应则表明，他认为 AI 应用的市场需求依然强劲。SpaceX 今年早些时候上市时披露，除建设地面数据中心外，公司还计划部署太空算力卫星星座，进军算力基础设施市场。此前，奥尔特曼曾指出，数据中心建设和算力需求可能存在上限，未必能够消化芯片厂商计划提供的全部产能。对此，马斯克 17 日晚间在 X 上作出尖锐回应，如果 OpenAI 的产品无法带动算力需求增长，就应该反思产品本身：“SpaceX 没有把 OpenAI 的任何采购收入计入预期。如果 OpenAI 的需求没有迅速增长，那就说明他们的产品有问题。”此前，奥尔特曼在 Semafor 举办的一场活动上表示：“我认为，市场需求和数据中心建设都没有问题。但我们不可能，也没必要把每一家芯片厂商提供的芯片都买下来。”马斯克则认为，即使没有 OpenAI 的订单，SpaceX 也能消化自身的全部芯片算力。他同样不看好新兴 AI 云服务商，甚至曾预测它们会落得“像孔雀鱼一样死去”的下场。与此同时，马斯克计划在 2026 年底前为“巨像”数据中心部署超过 120 万块英伟达 GPU，打造全球最大的算力集群。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，据 tom's hardware 报道，埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）旗下的 SpaceXAI（SpaceXSI）在美国密西西比州的 AI 数据中心发生化学品泄漏事件。承包商在连接移动储罐时因软管配置错误，导致用于数据中心液冷散热的传热流体（主要成分为低毒性的抑制型丙二醇水溶液，用于数据中心或发电冷却系统）发生泄漏。部分液体流出厂区并进入附近的排水沟。密西西比州环境质量部（MDEQ）介入了此次 SpaceXAI 设施化学品泄漏事件。经确认，泄漏的丙二醇总量在 5000 至 6000 加仑（IT之家注：约合 18.93 – 22.71 m³）之间。由于泄漏物质在 OSHA 标准下属于非危险混合物，且在自然水体和土壤中降解较快（通常数天至一周内分解），加之目前液体已被围堰拦截在排水沟内、未流入下游的霍恩湖溪（Horn Lake Creek），因此 MDEQ 称对周边居民的健康与安全无直接威胁。目前，相关工作人员正在清理现场并持续监测，以防出现进一步问题；同时，有关部门已确认将采集水样进行实验室分析。不过，由于该数据中心此前已因临时燃气轮机噪音与空气污染问题引发当地居民诉讼，此次泄漏再次加剧了社区对大型 AI 算力中心扩张监管与透明度的担忧。

articles.title: 《GTA 6》发售后 R 星总裁山姆 · 豪瑟罕见致谢：愿未来多年与大家同行
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，《GTA 6》终于来了，就连一向低调、鲜少公开发言的 R 星联合创始人兼总裁山姆 · 豪瑟，也罕见发表了一份声明，欢迎玩家来到雷奥奈达州，并对玩家表示“无比感激”。豪瑟向外媒 GamesRadar+ 发表的声明提到：“我们从创立之初就相信，游戏可以像其他叙事艺术一样获得认可，成为现代文化不可或缺的一部分，让其中的故事和世界长久留在人们心中。”“本周，GTA 系列重返雷奥奈达州，回到现代的罪恶城。虽然时过境迁，许多事情都变了，但有一点始终如一：我们希望创造超越玩家期待的游戏体验，展现游戏这种媒介究竟能做到什么，以及我们为什么认为游戏如此特别。”据IT之家了解，GTA 系列历代正传作品的执行制作人名单上都有豪瑟的名字。报道指出，作为 R 星创作团队的核心人物，长期主导游戏的创作方向的豪瑟深知，R 星庞大的开放世界对玩家意味着什么，也清楚重返罪恶城会吸引全球多少目光，因此丝毫不敢轻视此次挑战。豪瑟在声明中写道：“无论你是一路玩着 GTA 系列走到今天，还是第一次接触 GTA，你都将进入一个充满无限可能的世界。故事最终会带给你怎样的感受，又会迎来什么样的结局，都取决于你自己的选择。我们希望游戏既有熟悉的感觉，又能带来全新的体验。最重要的是，希望你玩得开心。我们期待，在未来的许多年中，继续与你们分享更多这样的体验。”

articles.title: 《GTA 6》无法重玩已完成任务，仅提供 15 个手动存档位
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，《GTA 6》有一个令部分玩家意外的设定：任务完成后，无法重新游玩已经完成的任务。这可能会让一些玩家感到惊讶，毕竟 Rockstar 直到上一代作品《GTA 5》中，都还保留着重玩任务的功能。但在《GTA 6》中，一旦玩家推进了剧情，就无法再回头重新体验之前的任务。IGN 的评测人员在超过 100 小时的游戏体验中，已经确认了这一点。当然，玩家可以利用游戏提供的 15 个存档位来保存进度。但考虑到游戏中的任务数量远远超过存档位，玩家必须仔细考虑应该在什么时候、什么位置手动保存进度。按照计算，玩家每完成约 6.6% 的游戏内容，就需要创建一个新的手动存档，才能充分利用全部 15 个存档位。游戏当然也提供自动存档功能。当玩家被警察逮捕（Busted）或角色死亡（Wasted）时，自动存档可以帮助玩家保留进度。此外，游戏中还会出现一些重要的剧情任务。玩家应该能够像在《GTA 5》中准备进行大型抢劫、《GTA：圣安地列斯》中迎来决战，或者《GTA：罪恶都市》中突袭黑帮头目豪宅之前一样，提前判断这些关键任务的到来，并考虑在开始任务前手动存档。不过，与此前的作品相比，《GTA 6》似乎也让玩家更难触发任务失败。《GTA 6》技术副总裁戴维 · 海因德（David Hynd）表示：“在这个项目中，开发团队采用了更加开放的设计理念。例如，我们非常希望减少玩家因为尝试不同玩法或探索其他可能性而导致任务失败的情况。同时，我们也希望鼓励玩家按照自己认为合适的方式，以及符合个人游戏风格的方式完成任务。”这意味着，Rockstar 重新审视了传统游戏机制的运用方式和敌方 AI 的设计，并对任务及关卡设计进行了调整，让玩家能够通过“多种不同方式”完成游戏中的每一项任务。海因德表示：“要让任务尽可能保持开放性，难度其实很大，尤其是在《GTA 6》这样规模庞大的游戏中。但我们认为，这种设计能够为玩家带来自由度和灵活性，一切努力都是值得的。”他还指出，开发团队希望玩家能够在游戏过程中逐渐理解并运用世界运行的一些固定规则，同时也希望玩家在发现某些规则有时适用、有时却不适用时，能够感到惊喜。IT之家注意到，在此前的《GTA》作品中，玩家可以随时找到并重新游玩已经完成的任何任务。以《GTA 5》为例，玩家只需进入故事模式，打开暂停菜单，依次选择“游戏”以及“重玩任务”，随后就能挑选想要重新体验的任务。但《GTA 6》的游戏结构更加复杂，这也是 Rockstar 决定采用这种线性进度设计的原因。

articles.title: 超 250 万人同时围观，《GTA 6》发售仅半小时创下 Twitch 单机游戏收视纪录
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，对于全球游戏行业来说，今天无疑是一个具有里程碑意义的时刻。《GTA 6》媒体评测正式解禁，这款游戏也成为有史以来评分最高的游戏。与此同时，评测解禁时间恰逢游戏在新西兰正式发售，当地午夜钟声敲响后，玩家开始陆续体验这款期待已久的大作。一些玩家选择通过调整主机时间等方式，利用时区差异提前进入游戏；另一些人则选择先通过直播观看游戏内容。IT之家注意到，游戏发售仅 30 分钟，《GTA 6》就打破了 Twitch 平台史上单机游戏最高同时观看人数纪录，而且看起来距离打破整个游戏类别的最高观看人数纪录也只差一步之遥。根据吉尼斯世界纪录此前公布的数据，Twitch 平台史上单机游戏最高同时观看人数纪录为 128 万人，由《霍格沃茨之遗》于 2023 年创下。然而，《GTA 6》发售仅 30 分钟，就以压倒性优势刷新了这一纪录。截至报道发布时，Twitch 平台《GTA 6》专区的同时观看人数已经超过 250 万，每位观众都迫不及待地想提前一睹游戏的真实面貌。其中，主播阿兰佐卡（Alanzoka）个人直播间的观看人数就达到 22.7 万。其他主播的表现同样惊人，xQc 和 TheBurntPeanut 的直播间观看人数分别达到 9.9 万和 4.8 万。Twitch 平台多人游戏的同时观看人数纪录，眼下也可能岌岌可危。根据 TwitchTracker 的统计，《英雄联盟》目前保持着 Twitch 平台多人游戏最高同时观看人数纪录，2022 年 11 月创下的峰值为 311.1 万人。目前，《GTA 6》的观看人数已经达到这一纪录的约 80%。值得注意的是，Twitch 最大观众来源地美国仍有近半数用户处于睡眠状态。此外，Valorant 目前保持着 Twitch 单日最高观看时长纪录，达到 3400 万小时。不过，考虑到《GTA 6》目前的火爆程度，这项纪录恐怕也很难维持到今天结束。事实上，在正式发售之前，《GTA 6》就已经不断刷新纪录，成为游戏史上预购量最高的作品，预购人数至少达到 1000 万。这一数据是在游戏发售前 9 天公布的，因此到正式发售时，预购人数很可能已经翻了一番。

articles.title: 2026 年苹果 App Store Awards 入围名单揭晓，含《燕云十六声》《潜水员戴夫》等
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 18 日消息，苹果今日公布了 2026 年 App Store Awards 的 45 位入围者名单。官方表示，这些来自世界各地的开发者所打造的 App 和游戏在技术创新、用户体验和设计领域均展现了非凡成就。IT之家获悉，今年的入围作品涵盖 iPhone、iPad、Mac、Apple Vision Pro、Apple Watch 平台以及文化影响类项目。获奖作品名单将在未来几周内公布。年度 iPhone App 入围作品《(Not Boring) Camera》：让 iPhone 变身为可自定义的怀旧式相机。《Raylie》：为每段飞行提供个性化导览体验。年度 iPhone 游戏入围作品《潜水员戴夫》：带玩家走上别开生面的深海探索之旅。年度 iPad App 入围作品《Cosmos》：通过营造精美氛围激发用户灵感。《Kiddopia》：为小朋友提供了寓教于乐的欢乐空间。《Mockup》：帮助用户设计心目中的网站或 app。年度 iPad 游戏入围作品《伊莫》：与超萌生物一起展开奇幻冒险。《明日方舟：终末地》：在遥远卫星上展开惊心动魄的战斗。《燕云十六声》：打造电影级武侠动作游戏体验。年度 Mac App 入围作品《Paste》：进一步强化 Mac 剪贴板的功能。《Things 3》：提供任务管理的简洁方案。《Ulysses》：助用户轻松创作风格精美的文档。年度 Apple Vision Pro App 入围作品《MLB》：以最佳机位现场直播棒球比赛。《Museas》：将客厅变成美不胜收的画廊。年度 Apple Vision Pro 游戏入围作品《Ping Pong Club》：为玩家带来酣畅淋漓的乒乓球体验。年度 Apple Watch App 入围作品《Moonlitt》：提醒用户关注即将到来的月相活动。《StressWatch》：报告实时压力水平。文化影响力 App 入围作品《Brilliant》：教授数学和科学的基础知识。《Unedo》：将学习西班牙语变成充满乐趣的文化之旅。

articles.title: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. articles.title: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. articles.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21827v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene-change split, the background stops helping and starts hurting. Accuracy is 22.8% on full chips and 30.8% when only the vehicle is shown. A SAR foundation model, SARATR-X, leans on the background more than ConvNeXt does (+4 to +6 points with the vehicle removed, in every seed) and does not solve the scene change. articles.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the best frontier models outperform human auditors (Fable 5.1: AUROC 0.73, 32% full identification) within noise and weaker models perform comparably. articles.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21885v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it significantly better. articles.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed proposals, and (3) they utilize features sampled uniformly from across the target layers, omitting important hidden states. articles.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21937v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open radio access networks (O-RAN). articles.title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21946v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change in which chains are still running. We measure both on MATH-500. articles.title: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21948v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The regulation of Artificial Intelligence is susceptible to various forms of capture by industry actors that hold undue influence over the policymaking process, due in part to their information advantage in developing these technologies. In the following paper, we investigate the roles of public commenters in providing evidence to potential regulation in the USA. We build a corpus of 40 potential regulations, and 2,664 public comments submitted by a variety of stakeholders. We computationally process these texts to extract evidence meant to inform regulators, in the form of formal citations and informal references. We find significant differences in the type and amount of evidence supplied: Holding comment length constant, business commenters introduce altogether less evidence, and government, university, and civil society commenters provide significantly more research and legal sources. articles.title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21950v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 ProteinGym baselines. articles.title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21978v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and budgets, while hosts distribute the public program and may retain private services server-side. articles.title: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. We specify the design: storage record, budget-derived retention, append-only read path, and bounded aggregation. articles.title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. Abstract: An expert who corrects a concept prediction, such as a BI-RADS descriptor in breast ultrasound, expects the diagnosis to improve. articles.title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21688v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool-using agents rely on execution harnesses to organize and schedule tool operations. The same task and resource description can conceal runtime conditions that reverse the latency ordering of valid execution plans. Resolving this uncertainty requires firsthand execution in the target setting. We introduce DeltaHarness, an execution-guided policy-search method that adapts agent harnesses from cold-start measurements. Its QHI loop uses the observed response to update runtime dispatch, revise physical plans, and select experiments for later proposals. An independent confirmation panel controls policy replacement. With fixed dispatch, a revised materialization policy reduces complete-delivery latency by 30.0% on one video-editing task across three fresh pairs. On held-out tasks, the evolved policies reduce latency by 8.2% relative to the best fixed plan in one seed and by 4.6% relative to the initial proposal in another.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21691v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rise of mobile devices equipped with numerous sensors, such as LiDAR and cameras, has driven the adoption of multi-modal deep intelligence for distributed sensing tasks, such as smart cabins and driving assistance. However, the arrival time of mobile sensory data vary due to modality size and network dynamics, which can lead to delays (if waiting for slow data) or accuracy decline (if inference proceeds without waiting). Moreover, the diversity and dynamic nature of mobile systems exacerbate this challenge. In response, we present a shift to \textit{opportunistic} inference for asynchronous distributed multi-modal data, enabling inference as soon as partial data arrives. While existing methods focus on optimizing modality consistency and complementarity, known as modal affinity, they lack a \textit{computational} approach to control this affinity in open-world mobile environments. %

Abstract: Acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) is essential for millimeter-wave (mmWave) multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21766v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Practitioners choose among LLM alignment methods largely by trial and error. We provide a theoretical foundation: each pairwise method defines a vector field on the probability simplex that governs how the model redistributes mass between preferred and dispreferred completions. Projecting onto a single preferred/dispreferred pair reduces this to a one-dimensional margin ODE with a closed-form solution. These solutions reveal that DPO margins grow without bound (logarithmically as $O(\log t)$ in the gradient-flow limit) while IPO margins converge to a finite $1/(2\tau)$; that label noise induces a qualitative phase transition in DPO (unbounded $\to$ bounded) but affects IPO only quantitatively; and that gradient concentration under asymmetric weighting governs trainability at scale. Abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. Abstract: Background: Crisis helplines are essential to mental health systems but are often understaffed and underfunded. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deployed LLMs field hundreds of millions of conversations a day and refuse a non-trivial fraction of user requests, yet the user-side cost of refusal, whether users disengage and by how much, is unmeasured on any production model: a blind spot for the consumer-facing platforms built on them. A/B-testing refusal is ethically and operationally constrained on frontier-lab products and unavailable to third-party platforms deploying these models through a fixed API. We introduce RAW, a method that uses LLM stochasticity as a natural experiment: at near-identical prompts in any existing log, the same model sometimes refuses and sometimes does not, and that variation identifies the causal user-side effect of refusal. arXiv:2611.21643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Estimating full-night electroencephalography (EEG) spectrograms from peripheral measurements could extend EEG-informed sleep analysis to recordings acquired without EEG. A block-autoregressive translator then predicts target EEG word identities and occurrence-specific duration refinements within fixed-duration blocks. Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel in vision-language tasks; yet, whether they maintain consistent understanding of information-rich visuals (InfoVis) when the surface language changes remains unclear. We construct seed-matched, language-parallel visuals and QA pairs by disentangling numerical-structural data from text and programmatically synchronizing translated labels. We evaluate 25 MLLMs under two settings: Language-Aligned QA (LQA, matching visual-text languages) and Cross-Language QA (XQA, fixed QA language with varying visual languages). articles.content:

Abstract: We present Limite 1B - Violetto, a one-billion-parameter model designed for high-throughput mathematical reasoning. Limite is trained from scratch on 237 billion tokens from a carefully curated, mathematics-centric corpus and supports context lengths of up to 131k tokens. Its architecture and training recipe were developed together to maximize reasoning capability while keeping training and inference costs low. Post-training combines knowledge distillation, targeted supervised fine-tuning, and RLVR on a curated curriculum. Limite achieves 94.01% on AIME 2026 and 74.25% on BeyondAIME, placing it among models many times its size on our evaluation suite. The model is deliberately only lightly instruction-tuned: it is intended primarily as a single-turn mathematical solver and as a fast, parallel component of larger systems, rather than as a general-purpose assistant. articles.content:

Abstract: Generative AI agents can help journalists explore large document collections. But exploratory workflows can require substantial token use and time, especially when the task is broad and the relevant subquestions are not yet known. This paper introduces FieldGuide, an agent-facing corpus map that organizes a document collection into a topic hierarchy and exposes tools for corpus orientation, scoped search, and bounded reading. Across the five tasks, FieldGuide used 27% fewer tokens and 41% less elapsed time than raw-file access; relative to RAG, it used 38% fewer tokens and 21% less elapsed time. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21648v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hoel (2021) proposed that dreams distort replayed experience so that the brain does not overfit to recent events. We test this hypothesis on an LLM agent (Claude Opus 5.5) that stores what it learns in a text memory and rewrites that memory each night from the day's conversation transcript. The agent goes through ten simulated days of conversation built from LongMemEval. We corrupt 5, 10, 20 or 40 percent of the transcript's turns before each nightly rewrite in one of two ways. Detail corruption changes one or two details in a turn to plausible wrong ones, or replaces the turn with one by the same speaker from an earlier day. Random-text corruption replaces half of the selected turns with a passage of Moby-Dick and inserts Moby-Dick words into the other half. Abstract: Sycophancy in large language models is often measured as agreement with the user, yet agreement can be appropriate when the user's claim is valid, their preference is genuine, or their experience warrants acknowledgment. We use this framework to analyze three sources of agreement pressure: human preference data, automated judge specification, and in-context personalization. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21651v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A controller that resamples an answer, escalates to a larger model, or abstains is usually justified by a confidence signal. Three claims about such a signal do not follow from one another: it ranks answers (discrimination), it supports withholding some of them (selective prediction), and it changes an answer for the better (correction utility). Abstract: Financial sentiment analysis is critical for automated trading, portfolio management, and risk assessment, heavily relying on models like FinBERT. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21669v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Masked diffusion models repeatedly predict provisional tokens before a sampler decides which predictions become permanent. Existing inference-time steering methods primarily modify activations, logits, or denoising trajectories, while treating this commitment policy as a fixed decoding detail. We instead study token commitment as a diffusion-specific control surface and separate it into two decisions: which tokens to commit and how many tokens to commit at each step. For the first, we introduce counterfactual target-aware commitment, which ranks unresolved positions by a mixture of model confidence and leave-one-token-out target contribution. For the second, we introduce calibrated adaptive budgets driven by target progress and confidence. Abstract: Realistic user simulation enables the study of human interactions when direct experimentation is costly or potentially harmful. To support this approach, we construct PSYCHE, a dataset of 18,576 profile-network pairs derived from 516 psychotherapy cases. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21878v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models are increasingly asked where real actors stand: what a party's platform prioritises, what an institution has committed to. Such judgments are gradable, carrying both an order and a magnitude. Nearly every benchmark that tests them asks about one entity at a time, then reads that score as the model's knowledge of the domain. Order and magnitude, however, need not be acquired together. Text about social entities carries far more comparison than measurement, so a model may hold a dependable ordering with no anchored scale beneath it. We ask whether a model can place a documented social position on a scale or only order the actors it compares, and what that means for how such knowledge is measured. Abstract: Automatic assignment of ICD-10 codes from short clinical diagnosis text is a practical medical text classification and normalization task. articles.title: Every Camera Grows Up: Camera-Height Regression in Interactive Video World Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21782v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Interactive video world models serve as simulators for embodied agents: from a starting image and an action trajectory, they generate the views the agent would see. The starting image fixes how high the camera is, for example 0.15 m for a floor robot or 2.2 m for an overhead camera, and a faithful simulator must keep this height as the camera moves. We show that six recent open-weight models fail to do so: as motion replaces the starting view with generated content, they move the camera toward human eye level, a failure we call camera-height regression. Our benchmark, EyeHeight, pairs six rendered elevations (0.15 m to 2.2 m) and four calibrated real-world rig heights with scale-free multi-view height estimation. All six models lose their initial height during a $180^\circ$ turn-and-walk rollout: initialized at 0.15 m, only 0-20% of clips end within $1.3\times$ of the starting height as inferred viewpoints converge to human heights of 1.

articles.title: Data-Driven Variable-Length Compression of 3D Representations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21802v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Compressing 3D shapes is important for the efficiency of many applications, yet existing methods either cannot leverage dataset-level statistics or use a fixed compression ratio for all shapes. We propose a learned variable-length compression method that exploits structure across a training dataset while adapting compressed representation size to individual shape complexity using only fast feed-forward inference. Our method operates on general latent representations and improves rate-distortion for both meshes and signed distance fields. Code is available at https://github.com/voilalab/varlen-3D.

articles.title: Sketch, Don't Paint: Allocating Test-Time Compute in Generative Visual Reasoning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21812v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal models increasingly reason by synthesizing pixels, sketching maze paths within interleaved chains of thought or rolling out video solutions frame by frame. Each visual thought runs the full diffusion schedule inherited from photorealistic synthesis, so iterative denoising dominates inference cost. We study how to allocate test-time compute along two axes: when to render visual thoughts rather than thinking in text or answering directly, and how many denoising steps each thought requires. Controlled interventions that vary only how the thought is rendered uncover three regimes. Causal thoughts carry the plan and become legible early: an 8-step sketch nearly matches a 50-step render in accuracy, commits to the same plan as often as two independent full renders agree, and in video models mostly fails by stalling short of the goal, so the rollout abstains. articles.title: Rethinking Perceptual Similarity for Remote Sensing: Multi-Layer Attention Scoring and Human Preference Benchmarking
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21816v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Perceptual similarity metrics for natural images transfer poorly to remote sensing (RS), where severe geospatial and semantic failures can remain visually plausible while still being decisively wrong for downstream use. To address this, we develop a novel human-aligned perceptual quality metric for generated RS imagery and evaluate it across several generation tasks. We first conduct a controlled perturbation study where we progressively increase the severity of common synthetic perturbations. Using the layer-wise Aligned Attention Score (AAS) responses in RemoteCLIP, we find that different RS artifacts are best captured at different depths. Based on these findings, we introduce Remote Sensing Perceptual Distance (RSPD), a pairwise metric that averages seven independently calibrated layer distances without tuning on human-preference labels. articles.title: Can a World Model Predict a Deepfake Video? A Consistency Margin Prior for Deepfake Detection
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21846v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deepfake detectors often perform well on the dataset they are trained on, but their performance drops when tested on videos from different datasets. In this paper, we study whether a predictive video model can provide a signal that generalizes better across datasets. Instead of relying only on generator-specific artifacts, as many existing detectors do, we use a model trained to predict natural video and measure the difference between what it predicts and what it observes in a video. Using V-JEPA 2.1, we keep the encoder frozen and adapt the predictor using rank-16 LoRA. We define the difference between the predictor output and the frozen encoder target as the prediction residual. We hypothesize that manipulated clips produce, on average, larger prediction residuals than authentic clips, and use this as our consistency-margin prior. articles.title: AR-WAM: efficient streaming world-action modeling for autonomous driving
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21851v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous driving requires anticipating how traffic will evolve while responding quickly to new observations. Video foundation models offer the first ability, but repeated history encoding and iterative video generation make them costly to use for driving. We present AR-WAM, an efficient streaming world-action model that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning. Because its video backbone is causal, AR-WAM updates its visual context incrementally, reusing past computation and conditioning future prediction on observed motion. We further hypothesize that future features computed from recent observations can improve generalization in dynamic traffic without iterative video generation. AR-WAM therefore obtains these features in one forward pass and uses them to condition trajectory generation, and reinforcement learning then improves the policy through direct optimization of driving rewards. articles.title: FaceRiff: Data-Efficient Unified Text-to-3D Face Asset Synthesis via Geometric Conditioning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21867v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-resolution facial datasets with consistent UV-mapped geometry, albedo, and physically based displacement are scarce, yet such assets are essential for photorealistic digital-human rendering. Existing 3D face generation methods are often slow, single-modality, or require large specialized datasets. Meanwhile, large image diffusion models encode strong facial priors but do not natively produce lighting-independent textures, pore-scale displacement, or UV-aligned geometry. We present FaceRiff, a unified, data- and parameter-efficient framework for generating complete 3D face assets (mesh, albedo, and displacement) directly from text in a shared UV space. FaceRiff adapts a pretrained SDXL backbone with task-specific LoRA adapters and uses UV normal maps as geometric conditioning: per-instance normals guide albedo and displacement synthesis, while a dataset-mean normal provides a canonical spatial anchor for mesh generation. articles.title: Domain-Tuned Diffusion Super-Resolution for 4K Facial Asset Maps
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21890v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Physically based facial assets require 4K albedo and displacement maps for cinematic close-ups, yet generative pipelines commonly produce them at only 1K. Naively applying photographic super-resolution is a poor fit: facial UV maps have domain-specific statistics, and displacement is a scalar height field whose errors directly distort geometry. We present a domain-tuned diffusion upscaler for 4x (1024 to 4096) facial asset super-resolution. Starting from a bilinearly upsampled map, we adapt a frozen SDXL backbone per modality with lightweight LoRA modules, while a Tile ControlNet preserves input structure as the diffusion prior restores pore- and wrinkle-scale detail. On held-out maps, our method produces sharper, more faithful detail than bilinear and off-the-shelf GAN and diffusion super-resolvers, reducing albedo LPIPS from 0.21 to 0.08 while avoiding misplaced or excessive displacement relief. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21892v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Label-free detection of viral infection is central to antiviral screening and pathogen surveillance. Most deep-learning methods analyze individual frames and do not model temporal progression. We evaluate temporal pseudo-RGB encoding, which stacks three time-offset brightfield frames ($t{-}6$ h, $t{-}3$ h, $t$) as the red, green, and blue channels of a single image so that morphological change becomes color and an ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN) can be trained on infection trajectories without architectural modification. In human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMVEC) infected with Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV) TC-83, a multi-task network predicts infected-versus-mock status and time post-infection in one forward pass. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21907v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual brain decoding from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data has made remarkable progress in recent years, driven by increasingly powerful artificial intelligence (AI) models and the growing availability of large-scale public datasets. However, despite the impressive advances achieved in static image decoding, the reconstruction of videos from fMRI signals remains challenging due to the temporal mismatch between rapidly changing video stimuli and the slow dynamics of the blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) response. We evaluate a Bayesian-inspired proposal-and-rerank strategy on CC2017 and the BOLD Moments Dataset (BMD), using a linear semantic decoder, a pretrained video generator, and three neural encoding streams with ridge readouts and learned pooling in two streams. articles.title: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Re-evaluating Adversarial Facial Privacy
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21923v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Published face-privacy methods report protection above 90% against black-box recognition models. That number comes from an evaluation protocol with two independent defects, reported in a measure that cannot size either one. The input is wrong: methods published since 2022 feed the network the whole photograph, or a detector's box, where deployed systems detect, align to a landmark template and crop. Re-scoring the same files through a realistic front end costs a standard transfer attack 56% of its dodging protection and a budget-allocating attack 7%, with no image regenerated. The measure is wrong: that loss is a difference of success rates, so it saturates, moving by 8.2x over a budget sweep while the effect beneath it moves by 1.34x. We therefore report the paired cosine shift, in which both thresholds cancel algebraically, so the input defect holds without committing to a calibration. articles.title: GridDriver: On-Board BEV-Based Language Planning and Reasoning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21924v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Bird's-Eye-View (BEV)-conditioned large language models (LLMs) enable language-interactive driving, but onboard deployment requires efficient perception and continuous planning alongside autoregressive language generation. We present GridDriver, an efficient BEV-conditioned LLM framework combining trajectory prediction, structured driving indicators, natural-language navigation, driving explanations, and scene question answering. Lightweight spatio-temporal BEV perception and spatially structured tokens provide scene context to a shared LLM, while frame-wise scheduling interleaves trajectory prediction with asynchronous language generation. GridDriver achieves competitive performance on public benchmarks, reaching 87.9% PDMS on NAVSIM and 57.6% accuracy on nuScenes-QA with a shared planning and QA checkpoint. articles.title: Does the Model Use What It Cites? Counterfactual Tests of Grounded Reasoning Chains in Small Video-Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21940v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A grounded reasoning chain cites a frame span and a box for every step, so a reader can check where the model looked. Whether the answer depends on the cited region is a different question. We test it by intervention: the regions a model cited in its own chain are blacked out, and the share of correct answers that flip is compared with blacking out boxes of the same size elsewhere on the same frames. The paired difference, the cite gap, needs no annotation. We apply it to 2-3B video-language models trained on exact CLEVRER chains and on pseudo-labelled NExT-QA chains. With the same weights, the cite gap is 0.089 on CLEVRER and 0.003 on NExT-QA. Pooled over models, masking the cited boxes flips 2.2 times as many correct answers as the control on CLEVRER and 1.1 times as many on NExT-QA, also among the answers that depend on the video at all, while the boxes pass a grounding check on both. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21945v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Making automated vehicles accessible requires consideration of vulnerable road users, including wheelchair users. To offer a more tailored experience that supports independence for this group, vehicle design needs to accommodate the wide range of wheelchair configurations. However, wheelchairs are individualized, varying in frame geometry, propulsion, and visual appearance. Moreover, occupants or accessories may obscure visual cues. Existing mobility-aid datasets only label the presence of a wheelchair, rather than describing its specific configuration. To fill this gap, this paper introduces the Wheelchair Configuration Image Dataset (WCID), comprising 467 face-blurred images across 192 capture groups solely for evaluation. articles.title: SCAN: Site-Aware Collaborative Privacy-Preserving Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for Neurological Disease Classification
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Worldwide neuroimaging data could strengthen diagnostic foundation models, but privacy rules often prevent centralizing brain MRI scans. We present SCAN, a site-aware collaborative adaptation framework for Neurological Disease Classification that lets new sites adapt a 3D medical vision-language model (VLM) without retraining or sharing patient scans. Each site keeps exact class prototypes for local prediction and can share privacy-protected class summaries: norm-bounded sums and counts perturbed once with calibrated noise. Using 7,641 scans from 67 sites across 12 countries, covering Alzheimer's disease (AD), stroke, epilepsy and controls, we assess local adaptation, cross-site benefits, and effects on existing sites. At seven unseen sites, the frozen VLM's zero-shot AUCs were 0.833-0.945 for AD and stroke. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21973v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A biometric designer controls the number of features and their temporal persistence. Earlier empirical work linked the equal error rate (EER) to persistence and to the required number of features by straight lines. We derive the law behind these regularities. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18702v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are vulnerable to adversarial visual perturbations, while defenses often require task-specific adversarial fine-tuning. We investigate whether robustness learned on source manipulation tasks can protect independently specialized target policies without target-side adversarial training. We first show that even a single source defense update improves robustness on held-out tasks, establishing cross-task defense reuse independently of multi-source aggregation. To combine source updates, we introduce Source-Norm Transferable Robustness Vector (SN-TRV), which retains the direction of their mean while calibrating its magnitude using source-update norms. The resulting update is applied to the target visual encoder without target adversarial data, target-side gradient optimization, or additional inference modules. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18855v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This report presents the design and implementation of Auriga Robotics' 1:10 scale autonomous vehicle, developed at Shahid Beheshti University's Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory. The platform integrates a custom mechanical chassis, a distributed embedded system based on ESP32 microcontrollers, and a Jetson Orin NX module for high-level perception and control. The embedded layer manages sensor interfacing, real-time data acquisition, and actuator control, while the Jetson handles environment perception through deep-learning--based lane, sign, and traffic light detection, as well as decision-making and trajectory control. System communication is achieved via structured UART links, ensuring synchronized operation between perception and control subsystems. articles.title: Passage-Focused Soft Coordination for Hierarchical Multi-Robot Navigation in Bottleneck Environments
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18877v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In multi-robot navigation, rigid global schedules are sensitive to execution deviations, while local methods lack long-horizon coordination. We propose a passage-focused framework combining soft global coordination with flexible local execution. A passage-induced graph of convex sets supports priority-ordered planning with two levels of soft coordination. Passage-aware route selection accounts for passage usage and traversal directions, while route-restricted continuous space-time planning penalizes temporal conflicts. The resulting references guide a model predictive path integral controller that avoids collisions online. Adaptive temporal and geometric tracking accommodates execution deviations, while selective replanning maintains coordination without rigid trajectory reservations. articles.title: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18919v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robots in homes, warehouses and farms must pick up objects they have never seen, usually without a 3D model or a category label. A grasping policy that works directly on the point cloud from a depth sensor needs only the geometry the robot observes, so it applies to any new object. Offline grasp generators such as Contact-GraspNet work this way, but they rank grasps by learned plausibility rather than by whether the grasp actually lifts the object. Reinforcement learning (RL) can optimize for that directly and make a point-cloud grasping policy much better on average, yet it leaves specific grasps persistently unsolved. We present a human-in-the-loop failure loop that targets those grasps: situations an RL policy keeps failing are mined automatically, sent to a virtual-reality application where a person picks the object up with their own hands, and returned to training as two grasp points. articles.title: Optimal Operating-Point Selection for Single-Linearization Trajectory Planning of Nonlinear Robot Manipulators
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Single-point linearization provides a computationally efficient basis for optimization-based trajectory planning of nonlinear robot manipulators. However, planning performance depends on the selected linearization point. This paper presents an offline performance-driven approach that treats the location of a single linearization as an optimization variable. Candidate operating points are sampled from a common cubic seed trajectory, and each corresponding affine model is used to solve an identical constrained finite-horizon quadratic program (QP). The resulting control sequences are executed on the original nonlinear dynamics, and the operating point minimizing the nonlinear trajectory objective is selected through grid search and bounded refinement. Abstract: Recent humanoid loco-manipulation in articulated environments has largely focused on geometry-dominant interactions, where success is primarily determined by geometric alignment and motion execution. articles.title: Robot Demonstration Videos Should Include Transparency Disclosures
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18982v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper argues that the robotics and AI community should adopt disclosure standards for demonstration videos. As physical and financial constraints limit direct public access to embodied AI, public dissemination of progress in robotics is mainly through curated demonstration videos rather than direct experience with the technology. In a large-scale (N=9,341), pre-registered experiment across six countries, we find that the general public struggles to discern both the visual authenticity (e.g., distinguishing real footage from CGI) and behavioral authenticity (e.g., distinguishing autonomy from teleoperation) of robot demonstration videos. The omission of these details distorts public perception, leading people to overestimate the ability of robots to perform tasks and navigate real world environments. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19034v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A frozen chunked robot policy can spend deployment-time inference compute in two coupled ways: more work within each policy call to refine a predicted action chunk, or more frequent policy calls to replan from fresh observations. We study this allocation without updating model weights. Our evaluation procedure reports success with both nominal compute rate and complete attempt cost, selects comparisons on discovery tasks, and tests prespecified comparisons on held-out tasks. Comparisons added after inspecting the held-out results only summarize observed patterns. We demonstrate the procedure with one frozen SmolVLA checkpoint in synchronous LIBERO simulation, using denoising count as the refinement control and fixing chunk length at K=50. articles.title: Certify, Then Select: Viability-Aware Runtime Steering of Frozen Diffusion Policies
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19047v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion policies, which generate short action sequences by denoising random noise, are a leading way to learn robot skills from demonstrations. Once deployed, they meet constraints the demonstrations never contained, and retraining for each is impractical. A safety filter edits the policy's action to satisfy them, but the edit ignores the task, and a large edit can leave the policy where it cannot continue. We propose CAST (Certified Action Selection at Test time): draw a few action chunks from the frozen policy, certify each with a barrier condition, and execute the certified chunk that a learned value ensemble ranks highest. Abstract: Integrating MLLM-based agents with robotic foundation models has attracted increasing attention as a means of enhancing robotic capabilities. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19100v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study supported reaching to extend a humanoid robot's workspace by bracing against the environment for stabilization using a straightforward yet capable whole-body model predictive control (MPC) approach, exclusively with local sensing and fiducial markers. While typical solutions for whole body humanoid control aim at avoiding or accommodating contact, contact is explicitly required to reach objects placed on surfaces far out of normal reach. We employ sampling-based MPC for whole-body leaning, bracing, reaching, and recovery on a Unitree H1-2 humanoid. The controller runs in real-time at 34 Hz on a laptop, transfers sim-to-real, extends reach by about 50 cm beyond the unbraced standing workspace, and sustains the loaded posture for over four minutes, before pose estimation drifts. Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable embodied artificial intelligence (AI) by translating visual observations and language instructions into robotic actions. Emerging use cases in physical AI are expected to drive the need for efficient inference and communication, as the computational demands of the VLA models pose challenges for real-time control with limited onboard resources. Test-time scaling through latent reasoning allows these models to refine hidden representations without generating explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens, but introduces a trade-off between task success, inference latency, and energy consumption. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19138v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous driving is turning to vision-language-action models (VLAs). They answer and plan by decoding, one step at a time. Each step is another forward pass, so a plan can take over a second of GPU time. Embodied AI often pairs such a slow, reasoning System 2 with a fast System 1 that acts. Human drivers plan at a glance, with System 1. Faster designs usually put System 1 outside the vision-language model (VLM), in a planner without its abilities. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19153v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recovering the forces behind a motion is ill-posed: different controllers can reproduce the same movement while generating different contact forces. Physics-based motion imitation resolves this ambiguity through simulation, but relies on fixed-gain proportional-derivative (PD) control. We show that fixed gains impose a trade-off between motion and force tracking, as contact and swing place conflicting demands on joint stiffness and damping. We introduce ImpedanceMimic, a reinforcement-learning policy that modulates per-joint stiffness, damping, and position setpoints from motion and force measurements, but requires only motion at inference. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19190v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can teach robot teams to navigate shared spaces, but trial and error causes collisions that real robots cannot afford. Control barrier function (CBF) safety filters prevent these collisions by correcting unsafe actions, yet in a team the filter becomes a centralized optimization whose number of constraints grows quadratically with the team size. We propose an approach that builds the filter's safety into the RL policy and examine how such a system behaves during filter-free deployment. However, the filter that keeps training safe also hides what the policy must learn: it masks the cost of unsafe actions, which actor-critic methods then overvalue, and it keeps near-collision states out of the training data. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19251v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning about what an action will cause requires internalizing how a system behaves. As conditions seldom stay fixed, this must often happen within a few interactions. Yet systems that look identical in a snapshot can respond differently to the same action, depending on physical conditions the snapshot hides. Context-based models capture this separation by summarizing recent transitions into a latent context, but do not specify how that context should change the equations of motion. Physics-informed neural networks build those equations into the model, but describe only a single system and cannot recognize when it has changed. We present Physics-Informed Causal Reasoning (PICR), which bridges the two. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19274v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks fail in ways that end-task success cannot see. HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark of ten hospital chores in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, each two unscored warm-up steps followed by a causal chain of five scored sub-tasks in one continuous simulation: the state one step leaves (an object pose, a choice, a fact seen once) determines what the next step must do, unlike benchmarks that place sub-tasks side by side. Vision-language agents act through skill-level tools from camera images. A scripted robot that makes only the calls a model gets is the solvability check of a chore. From each trajectory the benchmark reads where a chain breaks, what the agent did after a failed call, and how far its own position estimate drifts from the true one. articles.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
articles.content: Collecting large-scale, diverse, and high-quality post-training datasets for autoregressive language models is challenging. Consequently, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is typically applied to datasets significantly smaller than those used for pre-training, which leads to overfitting and the catastrophic forgetting of the tails of the data distribution. To prevent this collapse, we introduce Ambient SFT, a principled framework for leveraging imperfect predictions to augment the fine-tuning set. In our method, a "frozen" version of the pre-trained model serves as a noisy teacher that the fine-tuned model must match at a coarse level. In particular, we require that the high-temperature versions of the conditional distributions produced by the post-training model should match the high-temperature versions of the pre-training ones. The temperature hyperparameter controls the level of trust in the pre-trained model, with the limit $T\to \infty$ reverting back to regular SFT and $T=1$ to knowledge distillation. We demonstrate that our approach outperforms standard SFT across domain adaptation, instruction-tuning, and reasoning, leading for up to $21\%$ average relative improvement to standard SFT.

articles.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
articles.content: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. The reason is that recurrent layers combine all past frames into a shared state, so expiring old frames normally requires re-running the entire window through the model. We observe that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so the effect of each frame can be captured as a transformation that composes associatively. We present Spool, a training-free framework that caches per-frame state transformations and composes them efficiently as the window advances, removing expired frames from each recurrent layer's state without replaying frames through the backbone. Removal is exact within each layer; as with key-value eviction in attention, expired frames can retain residual influence through the cached inputs computed by earlier layers. We design a dedicated data structure and GPU kernels to achieve low caching and composition overhead. Across five open-source hybrid VLMs and four video reasoning benchmarks, Spool achieves the lowest p95 time-to-first-token in all 20 model-benchmark tests, reducing it by a geometric mean of $6.6\times$ over the faster of two recent vLLM baselines, while improving accuracy by 2.3 percentage points on average.

articles.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
articles.content: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality. We profile the inference pipeline of state-of-the-art models and find that operations often treated as fixed implementation details, such as VAE decoding and KV cache updates, in fact account for over half of end-to-end inference latency. We challenge the assumption that these components are indispensable and replace them with lightweight alternatives. Our 1.3B variant runs at 36 ms per frame, or 28 responses per second (RPS), on a single B200 GPU while matching the generation quality of a state-of-the-art model that is nearly 8x slower. Our 14B variant runs at 45 ms per frame, or 22 RPS, on an 8x B200 GPU node and yields significantly better visual quality and realism. We show that FastFrames enables real-time interaction in applications such as camera-conditioned and physics-conditioned video generation.

articles.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
articles.content: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools with specified inputs and finite domains, connecting tool use to textbook derivations. We illustrate these uses through specific questions, retrieved passages and finite calculations. The textbook collection and accompanying resources are available at https://github.com/xingyang-yu/StringQFT.

articles.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
articles.content: In this paper, we study a class of constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems. In many practical applications, all or some of the constraints are hard constraints that represent imperative requirements. Consequently, any desirable approximate solution must (nearly) satisfy these constraints. Motivated by this, we focus on computing an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, in which the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$, and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. While a recently proposed stochastic variance-reduced first-order penalty method can compute an $ε$-SFSO solution, there remains a significant gap between its first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution and that for computing an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, where both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are bounded by $ε$. To narrow this gap, we propose an inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient (SVRG) method that significantly improves the previously best-known first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution. Furthermore, when the objective consists of a single function, the proposed method reduces to a novel deterministic first-order method for solving standard convex conic optimization. It achieves a significantly lower gradient evaluation complexity with respect to the objective function compared to existing methods, and can outperform them when computing constraint gradients and projections onto the associated cone is cheaper than evaluating the objective gradient. Preliminary numerical results are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

articles.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
articles.content: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data. We find that sufficiently capable models do self-improve under these conditions, demonstrating strategies that align with classic cognitive frameworks for self-regulated learning and constructs from machine learning literature on self-generated curricula. Furthermore, we study the extent to which the learned text artifacts transfer to external benchmarks, observing improvement across different game horizons, mechanics, and 3D navigation.

articles.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
articles.content: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $φ= 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.

articles.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
articles.content: New coding models advertise themselves on score improvements of coding benchmarks. Yet no study has tested if a model that scores higher on these benchmarks gets more real work done. On June 12, 2026, a U.S. export control directive banned access to Claude Fable 5 for 19 days, which forced users to switch to other models. During this time, most former Fable 5 users switched to Opus 4.8 (11 points lower on SWE-Bench Pro compared to Fable 5). We treat this suspension as a natural experiment, where the people and projects stayed the same and only the model changed, so we could isolate the effect of Fable 5 on user productivity. We tracked GitHub pull requests of 297 Fable 5 users before, during, and after the suspension. We used 8,908 developers who stayed on Opus 4.8 all the time as the control group. We also repeated the comparison across five model upgrades before and after the suspension in 2026 (1,208 developers, 15,442 pull requests). Fitting a difference-in-differences model with developer and date fixed effects, we found that having access to Fable 5 increased the 7-day merge rate of pull requests by only 1.4 percentage points [-1.4; +4.3], which was not statistically significant. Similarly, no significant increases of merge rates were found with the upgrades (weighted mean: -0.9 percentage points [-1.9; +0.2]); all five estimates were negative (95% intervals included 0, did not differ from each other). We also did not observe a significant increase in the number of pull requests merged per week (+2.4% [-4.9%; +10.2%]).

articles.title: Feedback-Linearised Trajectory Tracking via Model-Informed Robust Geometric DDPC
articles.content: Data-driven predictive control (DDPC) predicts system responses from recorded trajectories, but nonlinear dynamics can limit the accuracy of fixed linear predictors. This paper studies geometric robust DDPC for trajectory tracking of a fully actuated manipulator using model-based feedback linearisation. A mechanical model maps virtual acceleration commands into joint torques, while recorded data capture residual dynamics arising from imperfect model parameters. The controller minimises worst-case prediction error over an open Grassmannian ball centred at the fitted trajectory subspace. Simulations on a planar 2R manipulator under gravity compare the proposed method with double-integrator model predictive control (MPC) and direct regularised data-enabled predictive control (DeePC). Results show improved tracking over double-integrator MPC despite increased torque effort, while performance relative to DeePC depends on the reference trajectory.
